content.comment_body: Hello, I'm attempting to set up the [product_name] to send email alerts (SMS works fine) for alarms in a new project, but email is not working. My setup includes: SMTP server: smtp.gmail.com; Port: 587; Encryption: STARTTLS if possible; my Gmail address and password. I found a forum post mentioning 'Allow less secure apps: ON' for the Google account, but it seems Google removed this feature after May 30. Is it still possible to configure email alerts, or is SMS now the only viable method? Thanks.

Hi, You need to enable the password for third-party applications in your Google account. Here's how: 1. Go to your Google account settings (the account for email sending), 2. Select security, 3. Set up two-step verification, 4. Google will prompt you to enter your password for verification and access, 5. At the bottom of the configuration, you'll find 'App passwords'—create one there. 6. Use the newly created app password in your [product_name]'s email setup so Google will allow emails to be sent from your account.

analysis.insight_summary: A user faces difficulties configuring email alerts on a [product_name] using Gmail's SMTP due to Google's discontinuation of 'Allow less secure apps.' SMS alerts function properly, but email setup fails. Another user suggests enabling two-factor authentication and creating an app-specific password as a workaround, revealing a need for clearer guidance adapting products to changing third-party service security policies.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects straightforward configuration of email alerts via Gmail SMTP on their [product_name], without having to adjust workflows due to updates in external provider security settings.
